# Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate is calculated using the number of unemployed people in relation to the combined number of employed and unemployed people—not everyone who does not have a job. Whether someone is counted as unemployed depends on their circumstances during specific survey periods.

In general, a person must not have been employed during the reference week, must have been available for work—with an exception for temporary illness—and must have actively searched for work during the four-week period ending with that week. A person on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled may qualify without actively searching, provided the other conditions are met.

Someone whose only job-search activity was browsing listings does not meet the active-search requirement. The distinction matters: availability, employment status during the reference week, and the type and timing of job-search activity determine whether a person is included among the unemployed—and therefore in the unemployment rate’s denominator.
